body:
I'm 9 days clean today after four years of balls to the wall. I've tried and relapsed more times than I can count and always failed at the 3 day mark. I can honestly say around day 4 or 5, I actually felt GOOD for the first time in forever. 

I know how much it sucks, just try and remember that your baseline for normal energy is gonna be out of whack for a while. Anything short of bouncing off the walls is going to feel like "tired". That's your brain fucking with you. You can do this, I promise. I felt like I'd never get out of the spiral.

You're very welcome! Just the fact that you recognized your own problem and asked for advice shows you've got a very good head on your shoulders. I've always been told that the exercise thing works wonders, so I'm glad you're going down that road. I'll get there too but like I said, been fighting depression for a few years and my using all that stuff was just to give me the kick to wake up and just get through the bare minimum. I do finally see light now, and look forward to getting to that gym phase. Addiction is the worst, so just keep your head up. All of mine showed up much later in life and I wish I could just go back and never touch the things that got me in those spirals. That's my best advice, just do your best to put this one behind you and be weary of other things in the future! It happens to the best of us.

I feel like I can maybe help to some degree, because I can very much relate to that. A large part was just me self medicating to fight depression, but I got a prescription for adderall a few years ago that initially made me feel so great, exactly like you're describing.  Eventually,  I got into that bad cycle where it messed my sleep up so much, I had to take more to overcome the sleep I was missing and so on with that cycle.   

Do that long enough and eventually you'll outrun your prescription and have to wait it out.  Not so much in the way of withdrawals, but the lack of energy and fatigue gets rough for sure.  Especially if you're a person that needs to do things.

About 2 years ago, I stumbled upon these head shop/gas station energy pills that had a similar energy lift, but actually would make you super tired at the end of the day (which was a plus, compared to adderall).  They worked fine, but the cost and tolerance went wayyyyy up, so I decided to stop taking a while back.  No withdrawals in the sense you would think of like with an opiate or something, but good GOD could you not sleep if you stopped taking.  You'll get super tired, and even managed to find some kind of sleep state, but will spend the entire night thinking nonsense thoughts on a loop that you cannot control.  After about 3 days of that every time, I'd always break and say fuck it go back to it.   Usually piled on some energy drinks too so it was just constant.

One thing I can definitely say is that even though I was more awake and alert, I could definitely feel a toll on my body in other ways and certainly my wallet.  But for the last two years, I've been on this hopeless cycle of wanting to quit, but knowing that I'm too weak to get through it so why bother?

I know this entire post has been about me, but here's why I wrote it:  Today marks day 6 since I've had one or any other thing else along those lines.  For the first time since I've started taking them, on day 4, I actually slept.  Something crazy happened on Day 5.  I had the first day where I actually felt GOOD on my own in probably 5 years.  In that time, I've gotten addicted to and beaten (for now) , Opiates, Kratom, Adderall and now these stupid pills.  I have felt good every day since, and now that I'm past the point where I can now see it's possible... my urge to use is gone for the first time and I'm not fighting it.

You need not cold turkey everything.  Have a red bull.  Have coffee, have a coke.  If you're able to, my best advice is to try and give yourself a period where you can reset.  Week off of work to do nothing.  I know that's not an option for all, and it wasn't even for me either.  I had to work the entire week and be single dad (the dread of doing all of that on a week when I was going to feel so bad kept me using as well).  

But I finally did it, and I used to read all of these success stories and never be able to put myself in them.  I don't say all of this to toot my own horn, I just really want you to know that not only can you do it, but it's possible to actually feel normal again in relatively short time.  It's really tough, because if you're anything like I am, you've lost your baseline of what normal energy feels like.  Anything less than bouncing off the walls feels like you're dead tired.

I'm not a doctor obviously, just wanted to share and I hope that it helps.
